headline: Application Support Engineer | Linux | SQL | AWS
summary: Cloud and DevOps Engineer who troubleshoots from evidence: decoded a live GitHub OIDC token to fix an AWS trust-policy failure, traced an AWS AuthFailure to clock skew from blocked NTP, and wrote 7 incident reports with root cause and actions. Runs an enterprise-style RHEL environment through tickets and runbooks; comfortable with Linux, SQL, REST APIs, logs in Loki and AWS.

bullets.text: Completed 30 hands-on labs across build tools (Gradle, Maven), Docker, Jenkins, Kubernetes, ArgoCD and Ansible, each documented with its objective, steps and verification.
Completed intensive hands-on training in Linux administration, networking, CI/CD, containerization, and cloud infrastructure, culminating in end-to-end DevOps projects (see Projects).

bullets.label: Automation & Operations
bullets.text: Idempotent Ansible roles (EC2 dynamic inventory) handle SSH hardening, SELinux, firewalld, chrony and fleet patching; Bash scripts rebuild and test the lab, with tickets, runbooks and incident reports documenting changes.

bullets.label: Identity & Team Policy
bullets.text: FreeIPA centralizes users, DNS, Kerberos, HBAC and sudo rules per team; the utility server runs a Squid proxy with per-team internet rules, NFS home directories, centralized logging and backups.

bullets.label: Infrastructure & Access
bullets.text: Enterprise-style RHEL environment on EC2 (VPN gateway, control, identity, utility and per-team workstations) in private subnets behind a NAT gateway, built with modular Terraform; reachable only through a WireGuard VPN with per-team ranges, firewalld and default-deny security groups.

bullets.label: Delivery, Streaming & Reliability
bullets.text: Trivy-scanned, Cosign-signed images are promoted by GitOps PRs and released as Argo Rollouts canaries gated on Prometheus metrics. Strimzi Kafka (KRaft, TLS/SCRAM, ACLs, dead-letter queue) carries events; Pytest concurrency tests, Prometheus/Grafana/Loki observability, and a disaster recovery drill rebuilt the cluster in 23 min 50 s with Multi-AZ RDS.

bullets.label: Platform & Security
bullets.text: Five Python/FastAPI banking microservices and an NGINX frontend on EKS, built for financial correctness (fencing tokens, row-lock ordering). Versioned Terraform modules deploy through GitHub Actions (OIDC) and ArgoCD App-of-Apps, secured with default-deny NetworkPolicies, Istio mTLS, Gateway API and External Secrets Operator (IRSA).
Streamed logs to CloudWatch Logs and set four CloudWatch metric alarms that notify by email through SNS.

Modular Terraform for a 3-tier AWS app (VPC, ALBs, Auto Scaling groups, RDS) with tier-isolated security groups, deployed through a Jenkins pipeline with a manual approval gate and monitored by CloudWatch alarms.

Serverless CI/CD for a 3-service app on EKS: GitHub Actions authenticates through OIDC with no stored AWS keys, secrets sync from AWS Secrets Manager, and ArgoCD keeps the cluster in sync with Git; monitored with Prometheus and Grafana.

paragraphs: I am applying for the Application Support Engineer role at Pyramid Pay in Cairo. I solve infrastructure problems methodically and document them so they stay solved. I bring hands-on Linux, SQL, REST APIs and AWS experience, and a habit of working from logs and evidence rather than guesswork.

The role centres on Linux, SQL, REST APIs and log analysis. In my RHEL lab I ran incident drills for an identity outage, a full log disk and a package rollback, documented in 7 incident reports with root cause and actions. I also traced a Terraform AWS AuthFailure to about 14 minutes of clock skew caused by blocked outbound UDP 123 (NTP), and fixed a GitHub Actions OIDC failure by decoding the live JWT. On the Nexora banking platform I built Python/FastAPI services on RDS MySQL, wrote Pytest integration tests, and declared 12 Prometheus alert rules each backed by a runbook.

Troubleshooting is the part of the work I already do every day: reading logs, narrowing a cause with evidence, fixing it, and writing the runbook. A support role puts that skill directly in front of users and production systems. I would welcome a conversation about how I can help your support team, and my CV is attached.

email_body:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Application Support Engineer role at Pyramid Pay in Cairo.
My CV and cover letter are attached.
I troubleshoot from logs and evidence on Linux and AWS, and I document fixes as runbooks and incident reports.
I would be glad to talk about the role.
why_this_role: Support work is the troubleshooting I already do: I decoded a live GitHub OIDC token to fix an AWS trust-policy failure and wrote 7 incident reports with root cause and actions in my RHEL lab.
